What’s your favourite trope?

Some stories stay with us because of the worlds they create, while others win us over with the tropes we can never resist. From second chances and chosen ones to unreliable narrators, time loops, and sympathetic villains and many more…there’s a trope for every kind of reader.

Swipe through to discover some of our favourite books built around these unforgettable tropes, and maybe find your next addition to the TBR.

Stories have always shaped the way we see the world.

They’ve taught us courage, heartbreak, hope, love, and loss. But what if the stories we grew up with weren’t confined to a single ending? What if every familiar tale held the possibility of becoming something completely different?

With Plot Paradox, we’re inviting you to look beyond the pages, to question, to reimagine, and to create.

This workshop is for everyone who’s ever paused midway through a book and thought, “I wonder what would’ve happened if…”

Come explore the art of adaptation, genre-bending, and storytelling that stays true to the heart of a narrative while daring to venture somewhere entirely new.

Starting: 15th August
Mode: Online

Forms will be out soon, stay tuned!

Welcome to IIT Kanpur, Y26s!

A new campus, a new beginning, and countless stories waiting to be written.

Whether you’re an avid reader, an aspiring writer, or simply someone looking for a community that celebrates ideas and creativity, Book Club is a place for you.

Here’s to meaningful conversations, unforgettable memories, and a year full of stories, both on and off the page.

Welcome to the Book Club family. We can’t wait to meet you!

Book Club presents another chapter of “Bookmarked Memories”.

This time, Kamal Raj reflects on The Power of Your Subconscious Mind by Joseph Murphy, a book that found him during one of the most uncertain phases of his IIT Kanpur journey. Amid the relentless cycle of placement tests, interviews, and rejections, its ideas became more than just words on a page; they became a source of resilience, helping him rediscover confidence, embrace uncertainty, and stay grounded when outcomes felt beyond his control. In this conversation, he shares how the book reshaped his perspective on setbacks, self-belief, and the quiet strength of perseverance.

Happy Reading!

Book Club presents another chapter of “Bookmarked Memories”.

This time, Soumya Thottempudi revisits the world of Percy Jackson and the Olympians by Rick Riordan, a series that sparked her imagination from childhood and continued to grow alongside her. More than a tale of Greek mythology and adventure, the books became a reminder that every challenge carries a lesson and every unexpected turn shapes who we become. In this conversation, she shares how Percy’s journey of loyalty, resilience, and self-discovery stayed with her through the years and offered a sense of comfort whenever life didn’t go according to plan.

Happy Reading!

Book Club presents another chapter of “Bookmarked Memories”.

This time, Sidharth Swaroop Mekap reflects on The Metamorphosis by Franz Kafka, a novel that challenged the way he understands identity, empathy, and belonging. Through Gregor Samsa’s transformation, the story offered a deeper perspective on loneliness, alienation, and the quiet struggles people often carry within themselves. It also sparked his interest in existentialist literature and introduced him to a community of readers who shared the same curiosity. In this conversation, he shares how Kafka’s work encouraged him to approach people with greater empathy and to look beyond what is visible on the surface.

Happy Reading!

“Love is never a single story. It is as diverse as the people who dare to feel it.”

This month, we're celebrating the stories that remind us that love has never fit into a single definition. Across kingdoms and classrooms, battlefields and quiet cafés, mythology and modern cities, LGBTQ+ romances have given us some of literature's most unforgettable relationships.

Our favourite LGBTQ+ couples are more than just iconic romances. They remind us that every love story deserves to be told, celebrated, and remembered.

Here are some of our favourite couples from Heartstopper, Red, White & Royal Blue, They Both Die at the End and more. Which ones would make your list?

Book Club presents another chapter of Bookmarked Memories.

This time, Rohan Batra reflects on The Midnight Library, a book that found him at the right moment. Amidst the uncertainty of first year and the fear of making the "wrong" choices, The Midnight Library offered a comforting reminder: every path comes with its own joys, regrets, and possibilities. Through Nora's journey, he learned to embrace his choices and focus on what truly matters rather than the lives he could have lived.

Happy Reading!

Book Club presents another chapter of Bookmarked Memories.

This time, Dhruv reflects on The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho-a book that has accompanied him through some of the most transformative moments of his life. What began as a distraction during JEE preparation soon became a companion he returned to again and again. From navigating homesickness and uncertainty in his early days at IITK to finding comfort in the idea of a Personal Legend, The Alchemist offered him hope, courage, and a sense of direction when he needed it most.
Through Santiago's journey, he discovered a reminder that dreams evolve, paths unfold unexpectedly, and the people who love us often give us the strength to keep moving forward.
In this conversation, he shares how the book became intertwined with his memories, the lessons that stayed with him over the years, and why its message continues to resonate even today.

Ha

In this edition of Bookmarked, Shriya Garg reflects on Sapiens by Sapiens, a book that challenged the way she viewed the world and humanity's place within it. From the idea of shared human stories to the realization of how much lies beyond our everyday concerns, Sapiens left her with questions, insights, and perspectives that stayed long after she finished reading. In this conversation, she shares a memorable quote, the thoughts it sparked, and how the book encouraged her to look beyond the immediate and think on a larger scale.

Happy Reading!

Book Club presents another chapter of "Bookmarked Memories".

This time, Shubham Maurya our ex-coordinator reflects on The Room on the Roof by Ruskin Bond, a novel that found him by chance and stayed with him through some of his most cherished memories. Through Rusty's journey of friendship, independence, and self-discovery, Shubham found echoes of his own experiences: late-night conversations under open skies, moments of quiet introspection, and the excitement of stepping into the unknown. In this conversation, he shares how the book became intertwined with memories of campus life and how its gentle reminder to appreciate life's ordinary moments continues to stay with him.

Happy Reading!

Ink & Insights: Underrated Books

Some books dominate bestseller lists and social media feeds. Others quietly sit on shelves, waiting for the right reader to discover them.

This month, we're celebrating Underrated Books, stories that may not receive the spotlight they deserve but leave a lasting impression on those who pick them up. These are the books that surprise us with their depth, stay with us long after the final page, and make us wonder why more people aren't talking about them.

From overlooked classics to hidden contemporary gems, we've curated a list of books that deserve a place on every reader's shelf. Join us as we explore stories that prove popularity isn't always the measure of a book's impact.

And here are our top recommendations for the theme.

As we turn the final page of this chapter, it’s impossible not to pause and feel the weight of every word we’ve shared, every idea discussed and every story that quietly changed us.

This journey was never just about books, but about the people who brought them to life. Stepping down as coordinators, we find ourselves reminiscing about the countless moments that made this experience so special, from starting buddy reads to publishing Mellifluous, from Halloween to the many discussions and conversations that stayed with us long after they ended. Together, we built more than just a club; we built a community, a space where stories connected us, inspired us, and gave us a sense of belonging.

To our secretaries and juniors, we couldn’t have asked for a better team, your dedication and enthusiasm made everything possible. To our seniors, thank you for your constant support, guidance, and bel

Happiness Happens by Robin Singh is a quiet, reflective read about purpose, awareness, and the responsibility we carry in our everyday choices. Instead of offering grand answers about happiness, the book gently nudges readers to pause and think about the kind of life they are building and the impact it has on others.

Through simple and direct writing, Robin Singh shares thoughts that feel honest and grounded rather than preachy. The ideas in the book encourage readers to reflect on what truly matters, from the choices we make to the purpose we choose to live for. It’s the kind of book that doesn’t overwhelm you with advice but slowly leaves you more aware than before.

Reviewed By: @nideesh.iitk
Designed By: @_ilika___

Note: These are our personal views and experiences with the book, which may differ from person to person.

Happy Reading!

Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions by Edwin A. Abbott is a deceptively simple descent into a rigorously imagined world where geometry governs society, identity, and thought itself. What begins as a clever satire inhabited by lines, triangles, and squares unfolds into a sharp critique of rigid hierarchies and the limits we place on perception. The narrative is playful yet unsettling, using mathematical ideas to expose how easily convention masquerades as truth.
